invent = to create something that did not exist before
invention = a new thing that someone has created
discover = to find something that was not known before
scientist = a person who studies science and does experiments
experiment = a scientific test to learn what happens
laboratory = a room where scientists do tests
device = a machine or tool made for a particular job
gadget = a small, clever electronic object
smartphone = a mobile phone that can use the internet and apps
charger = the object that puts power into a battery
wireless = working without a cable
download = to copy a file from the internet onto your device
upload = to send a file from your device to the internet
log in = to enter a username and password to use a site
password = a secret word that lets you open an account
username = the name you use to log in
social media = websites and apps for sharing news and photos with others
post = a message you put on the internet; to put it there
share = to let other people see a file or post
search engine = a website that finds pages when you type words
app = a small program on a phone or tablet
software = the programs that a computer runs
hardware = the physical parts of a computer
battery = the part that stores electricity in a device
plug in = to connect a device to electricity
switch off = to stop a machine working
print = to make a paper copy from a computer
save a file = to store a document so you do not lose it
delete = to remove a file or message
online = connected to the internet
offline = not connected to the internet
robot = a machine that can do jobs, often automatically
satellite = an object in space that sends signals to Earth
solar panel = a device that turns sunlight into electricity
headphones = something you wear on your ears to listen to sound
screen = the part of a device that shows pictures and text
computer = an electronic machine that stores and processes information
laptop = a portable computer you can put on your lap
tablet computer = a flat computer you control by touching the screen
desktop = a computer that stays on a desk and is not portable
keyboard = the set of keys you type on
computer mouse = the small device you move to control the pointer
touchscreen = a screen you control by touching it
speaker = a device that plays sound
webcam = a camera on a computer for video calls
microphone = a device that picks up your voice
USB stick = a small device you plug in to save files
hard drive = the part of a computer that stores files permanently
memory = the part of a computer that holds data while you work
processor = the part of a computer that does the calculations
operating system = the main software that runs a computer, such as Windows
file = a document, picture or other item stored on a computer
computer folder = a place on a computer where you keep related files
icon = a small picture on the screen that opens a program
browser = a program you use to look at websites
website = a place on the internet with pages you can visit
webpage = one page of a website
link = text or a button that takes you to another page
URL = the address of a website
Wi-Fi = wireless internet you can use in a place
router = the box that sends Wi-Fi around a house
broadband = a fast internet connection to a home or school
signal = how strong a phone or Wi-Fi connection is
network = a system of connected computers
cloud = storing files on the internet instead of only on your device
backup = a second copy of files in case the first is lost
update = new software that fixes problems or adds features
install = to put a program onto a computer
uninstall = to remove a program from a computer
reboot = to switch a computer off and on again
freeze = when a computer stops responding
crash = when a program stops working suddenly
bug = a mistake in software that causes problems
computer virus = harmful software that can damage files or steal data
antivirus = software that finds and stops harmful programs
hacker = a person who breaks into computer systems
password-protect = to lock a file or device so you need a password
privacy settings = options that control who can see your information
personal data = information that identifies you, such as your name or address
clickbait = a title that tricks you into opening a page
fake news = stories that look like news but are not true
influencer = a person who advertises products to followers online
follower = a person who sees your posts on social media
hashtag = a word with # that groups posts on a topic
emoji = a small picture used in messages instead of words
text message = a short written message sent to a phone
video call = a phone or computer call where you can see the other person
email = an electronic letter sent over the internet
attachment = a file you send with an email
spam = unwanted emails, often advertisements
inbox = the folder where new emails arrive
search = to look for information on the internet or in files
keyword = an important word you type into a search engine
QR code = a square pattern a phone camera can read
bluetooth = a way for devices near you to connect without cables
charger cable = the wire that connects a charger to a device
power bank = a battery pack that charges a phone when you travel
headphones jack = the socket where you plug in wired headphones
volume = how loud the sound is
brightness = how light or dark a screen is
screenshot = a picture of what is on your screen
stream = to watch or send video over the internet without downloading it all first
podcast = a spoken programme you can download or stream
blog = a website where a person writes regular posts
vlog = a video blog, often on YouTube
go viral = to be shared by a huge number of people very quickly
artificial intelligence = computer systems that can do tasks that usually need human thinking
chatbot = a program that answers questions in a chat window
drone = a small flying machine controlled from the ground
3D printer = a machine that builds objects from a computer design
virtual reality = a computer world you see through a headset
laboratory experiment = a scientific test you do in a lab
hypothesis = an idea you test in an experiment
results = what you measure or observe in a test
microscope = an instrument that makes tiny things look larger
telescope = an instrument that makes distant objects in the sky look closer
magnet = an object that attracts iron
electricity = energy that powers lights, machines and devices
circuit = a closed path that electricity can travel around
chemical reaction = when substances change into new substances
gravity = the force that pulls things towards the Earth
solar system = the sun and the planets that go around it
planet = a large round object that goes around a star
space station = a large spacecraft that stays in orbit and people live in
astronaut = a person who travels into space
research = careful study to find out new facts
theory = an explanation based on evidence, not just a guess
